notes:
`PRODUCT_VERSION` 1.0.1 · `CONTRACT_VERSION` 4.1.0

1.0.1 is about trusting what a run tells you. A reviewer is now handed the diff instead of being asked to go and fetch one, and grades it against a rubric that ships with toryo rather than one person's private dotfiles. A code-task checks whether the work it was filed for is already done before it plans anything, and says so plainly when it stops. And every harness resolves the same layered rule stack, so Claude, Codex and Copilot grade the same diff against the same standards.

### Added

- **Every harness runs on the same rules.** The shipped rules pack is retired: it reached no worker on any harness and described toryo's own repository rather than yours. In its place `toryo-directives` resolves a five-layer stack, lowest precedence first: your library's global rules, the project's library rules, your global files, the project's files, and nested ones. Both file layers gain a harness-neutral `.toryo/rules` home beside the existing `.claude` one. A Codex or Copilot worker used to run in a sealed harness home that loaded none of your rules while a Claude worker on the same step loaded all of them; the resolved stack is now seeded into each harness's own home, and Claude is given only the layers it does not already load for itself. `toryo-directives received <job-id>` prints the exact snapshot a worker launched with, layer by layer, including read errors and delivery status.
- **One review rubric, and it ships with toryo.** `review-task` and `code-task` told their reviewers that files under `~/.claude/` were the authoritative process and rubric. Those files ship with nothing, nothing checked they existed, and each prompt specified its output in enough detail that a worker which read nothing still produced a correctly shaped review from invented criteria, which the run then reported as a success. `toryo-library seed` now writes the documents toryo ships into your global library (setup runs it, an operator edit survives an upgrade, `--force` restores the default), each review step fetches the rubric by slug and stops the run when it is missing or blank, and the text is delivered inline. `library get` takes a slug as well as an id.
- **A run can decide the work is already done.** A `code-task` dispatched from ideas freezes those ideas, verifies each one against the freshly fetched base, and dismisses the ones that are already resolved behind a `path:line` citation that has to resolve. When every source idea is resolved the run terminates before a planner worktree is minted, having written no code. Runs now carry `outcomeSummary` and `outcomeDetail` so that ending does not read, from every list, badge and notification, exactly like a run that planned, implemented, reviewed and merged. Board shows which ideas are mid-verification rather than leaving them looking untouched.
- **Ideas have a second axis, and a ranking that uses it.** Effort can be set at capture (`ideas add --effort`, and an optional `effort` on the `idea_add` MCP tool), the nightly triage pass estimates one for every row that has none, and each axis records whether the score came from you or from triage. That provenance is what lets triage rescore its own guesses while never overwriting your judgment: before it, 288 of 332 open ideas sat frozen at the value a single sighting earns on the night it is filed, and the backlog had stopped ranking. Board sorts by impact per unit effort by default, renders both axes with their provenance (an unset one reads as unscored rather than vanishing), and scores a whole selection in one press.
- **You can sweep chosen ideas against the code, on demand.** `toryo-ideas verify-sweep --ids a,b,c` starts a verification run over exactly the ideas you name, with a Verify control in board's Ideas header whose dialog previews the batch. The nightly lane's 45-day idle gate is right for an unattended job and wrong for a person asking. The sweep also closes what it resolved: a `resolved` verdict at high or medium confidence whose citation checks out now dismisses the idea outright, and every verdict carries impact and effort estimates. Nothing is destroyed by a closure; the row keeps its prompt and its verdict note.
- **Board opens on something to do.** A first-run chooser offers guided paths, and the chosen one rides in a collapsible dock across navigation with each step ticked by a probe rather than a checkbox. The paths live behind the header's `?`, now a Help dialog carrying both the docs site and the chooser, so skipping the first-run modal is not a one-way door. The License dialog gains "Manage license", which opens the portal account screen.
- **`toryo-library export`**, which renders one document as markdown with a YAML frontmatter header, and an import that reads that same header back, so an exported file re-imports to an identical row. Board's Library panel can copy the markdown or save it to disk. `import` gained a `failed` count for files rejected for their own malformed frontmatter, which previously reported as a clean success.
- **foreman knows what is optional, what is busy, and how to say so.** ollama is now an optional service: a host that declined the install reports it unavailable rather than red, so `foreman up` exits 0 instead of leaving `foreman watch` respawning a missing binary every five seconds forever. A `restart <service>` that arrives while the supervisor holds the lease is queued for the supervisor to run once the service has drained, instead of waiting 30 seconds and exiting with empty output. And `up`, `down`, `restart` and `check` each print a short human summary on stderr, naming the failure, the stranded service, the dead supervisor and the queued restart. stdout is byte-identical, so every piped caller is unaffected.
- **Codex and Copilot jobs have a Cost.** Both are priced from the same shared, cited rate table Claude already used: an API-equivalent estimate of what the work would have cost against the model vendor's own API, never a claim about what your subscription was billed. A model with no published rate stays unpriced rather than showing zero.
- **You pick the model, not just the harness.** Each of `code-task`'s five roles accepts `<harness>:<model>` alongside the bare harness name, and an invalid pair is refused at run creation with the valid list rather than mid-run. Board's Ideas composer gained an Agent and Model pair with a per-role override. And on a host running more than one harness, the `sequence_run`, `schedule_create` and `dispatch_enqueue` tools now ask which one the work should go on instead of quietly choosing.
- **Sequences carry a description you can read and write.** The catalog shows it, the detail rail carries it whole, both authoring forms ask for it, and `sequence clone --description` gives a fork its own sentence rather than inheriting the one it invalidates. A single run can also be archived from the run detail panel, without selecting a second run you do not care about.
- **The hosted side.** The portal has password recovery, transactional emails are styled rather than plain, a marketing signup subscribes to the newsletter, and admin has a signups page.

### Changed

- **PR bodies follow one content contract.** Both the implementer and the self-review pass are given the same categories to consider (summary, motivation, design decisions, failure handling, deployment impact, verification with exact commands and measured results) and told to omit the ones with nothing material in them rather than filling them with `N/A`. A small change gets a short body.
- **`session-debugger` scores a duplicate read by coverage, not overlap.** It counted a read whose span merely overlapped an earlier one, while the guard it models denies only a read fully covered by what the session already holds, and it never noticed a shell rewrite. Both divergences manufactured findings for reads no guard would have blocked, and the first pattern to reach the ideas registry was made entirely of them. Re-analyzing an already-analyzed transcript will report fewer findings, and the `--duplicate-read-per-session` default moves from 2 to 1 to match the new floor.
- **A step's latest output is stored once.** It was written into both the step entry and the last history element, byte for byte, which was 11.1 MB of one store's 13.07 MB of history. The projection restores it on read, so nothing downstream changes and no migration is needed.
- **Board's Sequence screen dropped the registered-sequences table.** The design screen owns the catalog, so it was duplicate reference detail on the screen you open to answer "what is running".

### Fixed

- **A reviewer is handed its diff instead of acquiring one.** An acquisition that failed was indistinguishable from a diff with nothing in it, and one run produced three verdicts on a PR none of the reviewers had seen while every gate below it passed. The branch diff is now materialized into the run directory by a step with an exit code, and a second step fails the run if it landed empty. Three separate causes of the original failure are closed with it: a relocated Codex reviewer was denied the network its own prompt told it to use, an operator's `diff.external` silently replaced the output of `git diff` for every agent on the machine, and the reviewer had no reliable way to find its own checkout, so one of them wandered into a sibling run's worktree and graded the wrong branch.
- **A read-only step can write the artifact it is required to produce.** The reviewer was denied every write tool by name, while the file it had to produce was a matter of path. Claude survived by reaching for a heredoc no rule names; Codex, whose only write tool is `apply_patch`, was denied three times, ended its turn with the review composed in prose, and failed the step with nothing on disk. The deny set now lifts for a write whose every target lands inside the job's own artifact directory, which is the directory the sandbox already opened.
- **A Codex session can record its commits.** A linked worktree keeps its metadata in the parent repository, and neither path was writable, so a write-capable session could edit files and not commit them: one run pushed a commit to its PR and left local HEAD on the base. Those two paths are now granted to write-capable orientations only, and `code-task` gained a hand-off gate that stops the run naming both heads when the branch never landed locally, instead of failing four steps later with nothing to review.
- **Symlinked rule files are discovered.** Bun's file filter classifies a symlink to a file as not a file, so every symlinked rule was dropped in silence: one operator's global layer resolved 1 of 31 rules, and the Codex and Copilot runs that reach those rules only through directives were running with no engineering standards at all.
- **An update brings the schema and the shipped documents with it.** Both update paths now run the installed migrations and seed the shipped library documents before touching the sequence catalog, and report the failure rather than finishing green over a schema that was never applied.
- **Setup refuses stale assets that travel beside the binaries.** Run from an existing install, setup repaired the hard links and stopped, so a new binary sat beside the previous build's `migrations/`, found nothing pending against the database the old build had migrated, and printed a green migrations step over a schema that was never applied. `foreman doctor` agreed, because both sides of its comparison were stale together. Every asset directory now carries a stamp naming the build that filled it, setup repairs from a matching payload where one exists, and doctor reports a stale journal ahead of any conclusion drawn from it.
- **`claude migrate-installer` no longer reads as "claude not on PATH".** That installer publishes the binary as a shell alias rather than a link on PATH, so setup reported it missing on a Mac running Claude Code daily. Its directory is now probed, and the widened PATH is carried through to the worker's spawn.
- **Setup and foreman say what actually happened.** Setup's services failure reports foreman's own per-service detail (and keeps foreman's stderr, which is where docker's refusal actually lives) instead of an unconditional "everything else is in place". The launchd advice stops guessing at history. And setup closes with a "still to do" block built from what each step returned, including the case of a host whose entire enabled harness set is absent, which came up green and accepted work while every job died at its worker.
- **A clean approval no longer kills the run.** A reviewer approving a diff with nothing to report threw on the empty findings string, on a transform after the PR was already open, and a retry re-armed the same step against the same file. The guard now fires only where it means something, on a demand for changes that names none.
- **A run stops fitting its own state budget.** The artifact list a worker returns grows with the change rather than with the run, so a repo-wide sweep touching 1,813 files spent 97% of its state on it and died after it had implemented, self-reviewed and pushed. The list is bounded where a transform reads it and kept whole where you read it, so a run already wedged recovers on a plain retry.
- **The premise gate cannot close an idea it only partly answered.** An agent could cite a mechanism narrower than the idea, admit the gap in its own note, and still return `resolved`. Every qualifier in the frozen text is now part of the requirement, a remainder goes in its own field, and a resolution carrying one is refused and reported.
- **Board holds its state where it used to lose it.** The ideas brief rebuilds when the selection changes, rather than one hand-edit suppressing it for the life of the app. An optional enum selection can be cleared again. The archive stamp hides on a run that is still live instead of rendering disabled beside a reason the panel already gave. A foreman result banner can be dismissed. And an all-global dispatch into a project's root now carries that project rather than landing under no project, which used to fail the run after its PR had merged.
- **A base merge tells the implementer to refresh its workspace links.** An ordinary install can report no changes while the links are stale, which turns a healthy merge into an unexplained failure on the next typecheck.
- **A session that asks for the toryo MCP fails when it cannot have it,** instead of starting without the tools it requested and behaving as though they were absent by design.
- **The reviewer prompt reads the PR context it was written against.** Since the diff steps landed between them, all four of its conditional blocks had been rendering empty in every real run.
- **A project's library cleanup reads past the first page,** so cleanup no longer stops at the default 50 rows.
- **Signing in to the portal is fast again.** It was reported at 10 to 15 seconds; the path is measured at 249 to 266ms warm, and nearly all of the rest was fly starting an autostopped machine. A few sign-ins a day is exactly the traffic shape that leaves a machine idle long enough to be stopped, so a customer signing in once a morning met a cold start most mornings. Autostop is off, pinned by a test, and every leg of the path is now timed permanently.
